newsitem.title: USA: TI says free to focus on digital solutions.
newsitem.headline: TI says free to focus on digital solutions.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said Monday the sale of its defense-electronics business would give it the resources to push for rapid growth in the high-margin market of digital signal processing solutions.

"We expect to be a leading, premier electronics company focusing on digital solutions for a network society," Chairman Jim Adams told Reuters. "This allows us the resources to proceed, representing our shareholders, toward that strategy."
Texas Instruments is selling its defense business to Raytheon Co for $2.95 billion cash.
"This frees us up to look to our future," Adams said.
He refused to say if TI plans to make acquisitions with the proceeds from the Raytheon deal.
Shares of TI rose 1-7/8 to 68-3/4 while Raytheon was up 5/8 to 50-5/8 in morning trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
TI's defense-electronics division had revenues of about $1.8 billion in 1996.
Some analysts previously expressed concern that the Dallas-based company might become overly exposed to the volatile market in memory chips if it got rid of its defense division.
But Adams said this was not a problem.

"We have always been exposed to the volatility of the memory market, but obviously we considered all the factors in making this decision and it came out as a win-win for us," he said. "It positions TI well for the future. We are not concerned."
Adams said rapid consolidation in the U.S. defense industry has seen the big players get bigger by buying up subcontractors and smaller specialist firms.
"That is the direction of the industry...In the future, as the industry moves forward, the larger companies are going to have better opportunities in the marketplace," he said.
TI's defense unit, which has seen revenues grow only moderately in the 1990s, was not large enough to grow rapidly by itself and would be better positioned once united with Raytheon, Adams said.
